# Fixture generators

See [fixture generation](../../../docs/development/fixture-generation.md) for
the contributor workflow. This README remains part of the evidence chain.

## Lab captures on macOS (tcpdump sidecar)

Docker Desktop runs containers inside a Linux VM. Host `tcpdump` on `en0` only
sees the VM uplink, never container-to-container traffic.

For lab fixtures (Postfix/Dovecot/Cyrus + `openssl s_client`, Step 1+):

1. Create a user-defined Docker bridge network.
2. Attach the mail-server containers to that network.
3. Attach a `nicolaka/netshoot`-style sidecar to the *same* network with
   `--cap-add=NET_RAW --cap-add=NET_ADMIN`.
4. Run `tcpdump` in the sidecar against the bridge, not on the macOS host.

## Step 1

Scapy degradation cases are generated by
`tcp_degradation_captures.py --case <id>` (or `--case all`). Each case writes
`tests/fixtures/<case_id>/capture.pcapng` plus `provenance.json`.

The clean SMTP baseline is a **lab** capture, not a public Wireshark sample.
`lab_smtp_tcp_baseline.py` starts a plaintext SMTP server and client on a Docker
bridge and captures with a dumpcap sidecar attached to the server network
namespace (`--network container:<server>`), which is the tcpdump-sidecar
pattern from the section above. Public-corpus traces are not Step 1 proof
fixtures.

## Step 2

Lab cases (SMTP submission/587, IMAP/143, POP3/110) are generated by
`lab_mail_protocol_captures.py --case <id>` (or `--case all`). Each case uses the
same dumpcap-sidecar pattern as the Step 1 SMTP baseline.

Scapy identification cases (nonstandard ports plus one ambiguous banner) are
generated by `scapy_protocol_captures.py --case <id>` (or `--case all`).

Public-corpus SMTP and IMAP regression captures are imported by
`import_public_corpus.py --case <id>`. The script pins the upstream URL and
source SHA-256, then converts with `editcap -F pcapng` without otherwise
altering packets. These traces are regression only; they are not the sole proof
of identification.

SMTP on TCP/25 reuses the immutable Step 1 capture
`tests/fixtures/tcp_smtp_clean_baseline/`.

## Step 3

Lab STARTTLS success, implicit TLS with negotiated ALPN, and TLS-on-mail-port
without ALPN are generated by `lab_starttls_captures.py --case <id>`. Each case
uses the dumpcap-sidecar pattern and a throwaway TLS certificate minted by the
generator.

Adversarial STARTTLS/STLS cases (rejection, capability stripping, mid-transition
violation, plaintext credentials after a failed upgrade) are generated by
`scapy_starttls_captures.py --case <id>`. Advertised-but-never-requested
behaviour reuses the Step 2 nonstandard-port Scapy fixtures.

Public-corpus STARTTLS/STLS regression slices are imported by
`import_public_corpus.py --case <id>`. These traces are regression only; they
are not the sole proof of a rule.

## Step 4

Lab TLS 1.2 ECDHE, TLS 1.3 full handshake, HelloRetryRequest, and PSK-only
resumption are generated by `lab_tls_handshake_captures.py --case <id>`. Each
case uses the dumpcap-sidecar pattern on TCP/4433.

Static RSA, static ECDH, and RC4 are generated by
`lab_legacy_openssl_captures.py --case <id>` against a pinned OpenSSL 1.0.2u
image built from `legacy_openssl.Dockerfile`. Extraction only; policy judgment
is Step 7.

Scapy edge cases (`supported_versions` vs legacy record version, truncated
ClientHello) are generated by `scapy_tls_edge_captures.py --case <id>`.

Independent TLS 1.2 / TLS 1.3 public-corpus slices are imported by
`import_tls_public_corpus.py --case <id>` from The Ultimate PCAP (pinned URL and
source SHA-256). Regression only; not the sole proof of a rule.

## Step 5

Lab certificate-matrix captures (valid current RSA-2048/SHA-256, expired
RSA-1024, not-yet-valid, ECDSA P-256, SHA-1-signed, expiry-warning window) are
generated by `lab_cert_captures.py --case <id>`. Each case uses the
dumpcap-sidecar pattern on TCP/4433. RSA-1024 and SHA-1 are facts only; policy
judgment is Step 7. `cert_expiry_warning` also writes `analyze.json` so the
fixture harness freezes `--analysis-time`.

The malformed/truncated Certificate message is generated by
`scapy_cert_malformed_captures.py --case cert_malformed_asn1`.

An independent full-chain TLS 1.2 public-corpus slice is imported by
`import_cert_public_corpus.py --case cert_chain_public_corpus` from The Ultimate
PCAP. Regression only; not the sole proof of a rule.

## Step 6

Lab chain-validation captures (trusted throwaway-CA chain, self-signed leaf,
missing intermediate, SAN match, SAN mismatch) are generated by
`lab_chain_captures.py --case <id>`. Each case uses the dumpcap-sidecar pattern
on TCP/4433. The lab root public certificate is pinned in
`src/securemail/adapters/pki/trust-store-snapshot.pem`; private keys stay in
the generator. `cert_chain_san_mismatch` sends SNI `wrong.example.test` against
SAN `securemail.test`.

`cert_chain_public_corpus` reuses the Step 5 public-corpus capture.

## Step 7

Lab policy-boundary captures (TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1, NULL, export, SHA-1
CertificateVerify, RSA-1536) are generated by
`lab_policy_boundary_captures.py --case <id>` against the pinned OpenSSL 1.0.2u
image. Do not rewrite `lab_legacy_openssl_captures.py`; that script is already
named by earlier provenance.

The TLS 1.2 static-DH ServerHello is generated by
`scapy_policy_boundary_captures.py --case tls12_static_dh`.

## Step 0

`empty_capture.py` crafts a handful of unrelated (non-mail) packets with Scapy
and writes `tests/fixtures/empty/capture.pcapng`.
